lesson.subtitle: Lesson 1 -- The Dream: Why Harvard
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Gabriel Fernandes | Lesson 1 -- The Dream: Why Harvard

listenings.text: People ask me what we look for, and they always expect a number. The truth is that the grades only get your file opened. After that, we are reading for something else. We want to know what you did when nobody was making you do it. A boy last year ran a small business at a street market with his neighbour, and he wrote about the week he lost money. That page told me more than any test score. So do not send us a list of everything you have ever won. Send us one thing you actually built, and tell us what it cost you.

I am in my second year here, and I came from Sao Paulo. If somebody had told me at eleven that I would be sitting in this library, I would have laughed. The hardest part was not the English. It was learning to write slowly. At home I answered fast, because answering fast was how you looked clever. Here nobody is impressed by fast. They read what you wrote, and they ask you why you chose that word and not another one. If I could go back and change one habit, I would read my own sentences out loud before sending them. That single thing would have saved me a whole term.

extra_audio.text: My name is Gabriel and I am eleven years old. I want to study in the United States, and I have wanted that for a long time. If I got a place at a university like that, I would study law first. After my degree, I would train as a pilot in France. That is the plan, and I am starting with my English.
